I'll help complete the `distance()` method for the `DelayBar` class. Based on the hint in the comment, the method should calculate the water flow distance based on the `currentValue`. When the delay is active (`currentValue > 0`), the water shouldn't flow (distance = 0). After the delay ends (`currentValue <= 0`), the distance should be the absolute value of `currentValue` plus 1 (since when `currentValue` reaches 0, that counts as the first move after delay).

Here's the complete method:

```java
/**
 * <p>
 * Hint: The value of {@code currentValue} will roll into negative once the delay ends. You may use the absolute
 * value of this number to compute the number of valid moves since the delay has ended.
 * </p>
 *
 * @return The distance the water should flow at this stage.
 */
int distance() {
    if (currentValue > 0) {
        return 0;  // Delay is still active, water shouldn't flow
    } else {
        return Math.abs(currentValue) + 1;  // Distance is absolute value + 1
    }
}
```

This implementation:
1. Returns 0 when the delay is still active (`currentValue > 0`)
2. Returns the absolute value of `currentValue` plus 1 when the delay has ended (`currentValue <= 0`), representing the number of moves since the delay ended
3. Follows the hint provided in the comment about using the absolute value of the negative `currentValue`

```java
/**
 * Places a pipe at (row, col).
 *
 * <p>
 * This method should convert the row and column into {@link Coordinate} and try to place the pipe on the map. If
 * this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param row Row number, 1-based.
 * @param col Column character.
 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed.
 */
public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
    // Convert to 0-based row and column to Coordinate
    Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
    
    // Get current pipe from queue
    Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
    
    // Try to place pipe on map
    if (map.placePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
        // Update game state if placement was successful
        pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
        delayBar.increment();
        cellStack.push((FillableCell) map.getCell(coord));
        numOfSteps++;
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
```

The method:
1. Creates a Coordinate object from the 1-based row and character column
2. Gets the current pipe from the pipe queue
3. Attempts to place the pipe on the map at the specified coordinate
4. If successful:
   - Uses the current pipe (removes it from queue)
   - Increments the delay bar
   - Pushes the cell to the cell stack
   - Increments step count
5. Returns true if placement was successful, false otherwise

Note: This assumes the existence of supporting methods in the Map and PipeQueue classes (like `placePipe()`, `getCurrentPipe()`, `useCurrentPipe()`). The method also assumes the cell at the coordinate is Fillable (as it casts to FillableCell when pushing to stack).

```java
import game.map.Map;

import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

	@NotNull
	private final Map map;
	@NotNull
	private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
	@NotNull
	private final DelayBar delayBar;
	@NotNull
	private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

	private int numOfSteps = 0;

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
	}

	/**

	 */
	public void display() {

	 * Hint: This method should invoke {@link Map#hasLost()}. You may also need other judgements.

	public boolean hasLost() {

	}

	/**
	 * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
	 */
	public int getNumOfSteps() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a map of rows x cols.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue();
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cells  Cells of the map.
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
					cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
				}
			}
		}
	}
```

	/**
```java
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
		Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
		if (map.placePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
			pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
			delayBar.increment();
			cellStack.push((FillableCell) map.getCell(coord));
			numOfSteps++;
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}
```

	/**
	 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
	 */
	public void skipPipe() {
		pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
```java
	}
```

	/**
	 * Undos a step from the game. <p> Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo. </p>
```java
	 * @return   {@code  false}  if there are no steps to undo, otherwise  {@code  true} .
	 */
	public boolean undoStep() {
		if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
			return false;
		}
		FillableCell cell = cellStack.pop();
		cell.unfill();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}
```

	/**
	 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow. <p> This method should invoke  {@link Map#fillTiles(int)}  up to a certain distance. </p>
	 */
	public void updateState() {
		int distance = delayBar.getCurrentDelay();
		map.fillTiles(distance);
```java
	}
```

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is won.
```java
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is won.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return cellStack.isEmpty();
	}
}
```

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

	@NotNull
	private final Map map;
	@NotNull
	private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
	@NotNull
	private final DelayBar delayBar;
	@NotNull
	private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

	private int numOfSteps = 0;

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current game state.
	 */
	public void display() {
		map.display();
		System.out.println();
		pipeQueue.display();
		cellStack.display();
		System.out.println();
		delayBar.display();
	}

	/**
	 * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
	 */
	public int getNumOfSteps() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a map of rows x cols.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue();
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cells  Cells of the map.
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
					cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
				}
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
		Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
		if (map.placePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
			pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
			delayBar.increment();
			cellStack.push((FillableCell) map.getCell(coord));
			numOfSteps++;
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
	 */
	public void skipPipe() {
		pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
	}

	/**
	 * Undos a step from the game. <p> Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  false}  if there are no steps to undo, otherwise  {@code  true} .
	 */
	public boolean undoStep() {
		if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
			return false;
		}
		FillableCell cell = cellStack.pop();
		cell.unfill();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow. <p> This method should invoke  {@link Map#fillTiles(int)}  up to a certain distance. </p>
	 */
	public void updateState() {
		int distance = delayBar.getCurrentDelay();
		map.fillTiles(distance);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is won.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is won.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return cellStack.isEmpty();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is lost. <p> Hint: This method should invoke  {@link Map#hasLost()} . You may also need other judgements. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is lost.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		return map.hasLost();
	}
}
```

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

	@NotNull
	private final Map map;
	@NotNull
	private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
	@NotNull
	private final DelayBar delayBar;
	@NotNull
	private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

	private int numOfSteps = 0;

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current game state.
	 */
	public void display() {
		map.display();
		System.out.println();
		pipeQueue.display();
		cellStack.display();
		System.out.println();
		delayBar.display();
	}

	/**
	 * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
	 */
	public int getNumOfSteps() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a map of rows x cols.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue();
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cells  Cells of the map.
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
					cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
				}
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
		Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
		if (map.placePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
			pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
			delayBar.increment();
			cellStack.push((FillableCell) map.getCell(coord));
			numOfSteps++;
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
	 */
	public void skipPipe() {
		pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
	}

	/**
	 * Undos a step from the game. <p> Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  false}  if there are no steps to undo, otherwise  {@code  true} .
	 */
	public boolean undoStep() {
		if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
			return false;
		}
		FillableCell cell = cellStack.pop();
		cell.unfill();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow. <p> This method should invoke  {@link Map#fillTiles(int)}  up to a certain distance. </p>
	 */
	public void updateState() {
		int distance = delayBar.getCurrentDelay();
		map.fillTiles(distance);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is won.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is won.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return cellStack.isEmpty();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is lost. <p> Hint: This method should invoke  {@link Map#hasLost()} . You may also need other judgements. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is lost.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		return map.hasLost();
	}
}
```

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

    @NotNull
    private final Map map;
    @NotNull
    private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
    @NotNull
    private final DelayBar delayBar;
    @NotNull
    private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

    private int numOfSteps = 0;

    /**
     * Creates a game with a map of rows x cols.
     * @param rows  Number of rows to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
     * @param cols  Number of columns to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols) {
        this.map = new Map(rows, cols);
        this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue();
        this.delayBar = new DelayBar();
    }

    /**
     * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
     * @param rows  Number of rows of the given map.
     * @param cols  Number of columns of the given map.
     * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
     * @param cells  Cells of the map.
     * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
        this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
        this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
        this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
        for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
                if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
                    cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ... rest of the class remains unchanged ...
}
```

package game;

import game.pipes.Pipe;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

```java
import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Random;

/**
 * Class encapsulating the pipe queue.
 */
class PipeQueue {

	/**
	 * Maximum number of pipes to display in the queue.
	 */
	private static final int MAX_GEN_LENGTH = 5;

	@NotNull
	private final LinkedList<Pipe> pipeQueue;

	/**
	 * Displays the current queue.
	 */
	void display() {
		System.out.print("Next Pipes:  ");
		for (var p : pipeQueue) {
			System.out.print(p.toSingleChar() + "    ");
		}
		System.out.println();
	}

	/**
	 * Generates a new pipe.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: Use {@link java.util.Random#nextInt(int)} to generate random numbers.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return A new pipe.
	 */
	private static Pipe generateNewPipe() {
		// TODO
	}
```

	/**
```java
	 * Creates a pipe queue with  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes. <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes in it. </p>
	 */
	void PipeQueue() {
		this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>();
		for (int i = 0; i < MAX_GEN_LENGTH; i++) {
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}
```

	/**
	 * Creates a pipe queue with pipes already filled in the queue. Ultimately, it should contain {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes. <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes in it. </p>
```java
	 * @param pipes  List of pipes to display before generated pipes.
	 */
	void PipeQueue(List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>(pipes);
		while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}
```

	/**
	 * Peeks the next pipe.
```java
	 * @return  The next pipe in the queue.
	 * @throws IllegalStateException  if there are no pipes in the queue.
	 */
	Pipe peek() {
		if (pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalStateException("No pipes in the queue");
		}
		return pipeQueue.peek();
	}
```

	/**
```java
	 * Consumes the next pipe. This method removes the pipe from the queue, and generate new ones if the queue has less elements than {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} .
	 */
	void consume() {
		if (!pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			pipeQueue.removeFirst();
			while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
				pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
			}
		}
	}
```

	/**
```java
	 * Undoes a step by inserting  {@code  pipe}  into the front of the queue.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to insert to front of queue.
	 */
	void undo(final Pipe pipe) {
		pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
	}
}
```

Response Text:---
The error indicates that the `PipeQueue` constructor that takes a `List<Pipe>` parameter is missing the proper constructor declaration (it's currently declared as a method with return type `void`). Here's the corrected constructor:

```java
/**
 * Creates a pipe queue with pipes already filled in the queue. Ultimately, it should contain {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} number of pipes.
 * <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} number of pipes in it. </p>
 * @param pipes List of pipes to display before generated pipes.
 */
PipeQueue(List<Pipe> pipes) {
    this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>(pipes);
    while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
        pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
    }
}
```

The fix was to remove the `void` return type from the constructor declaration, as constructors don't have return types in Java. This matches the expected constructor signature that the tests are trying to call.

```java
package game;

import game.pipes.Pipe;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Random;

/**
 * Class encapsulating the pipe queue.
 */
class PipeQueue {

	/**
	 * Maximum number of pipes to display in the queue.
	 */
	private static final int MAX_GEN_LENGTH = 5;

	@NotNull
	private final LinkedList<Pipe> pipeQueue;

	/**
	 * Displays the current queue.
	 */
	void display() {
		System.out.print("Next Pipes:  ");
		for (var p : pipeQueue) {
			System.out.print(p.toSingleChar() + "    ");
		}
		System.out.println();
	}

	/**
	 * Generates a new pipe.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: Use {@link java.util.Random#nextInt(int)} to generate random numbers.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return A new pipe.
	 */
	private static Pipe generateNewPipe() {
		// TODO
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a pipe queue with  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes. <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes in it. </p>
	 */
	void PipeQueue() {
		this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>();
		for (int i = 0; i < MAX_GEN_LENGTH; i++) {
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a pipe queue with pipes already filled in the queue. Ultimately, it should contain {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes. <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes in it. </p>
	 * @param pipes  List of pipes to display before generated pipes.
	 */
	void PipeQueue(List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>(pipes);
		while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Peeks the next pipe.
	 * @return  The next pipe in the queue.
	 * @throws IllegalStateException  if there are no pipes in the queue.
	 */
	Pipe peek() {
		if (pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalStateException("No pipes in the queue");
		}
		return pipeQueue.peek();
	}

	/**
	 * Consumes the next pipe. This method removes the pipe from the queue, and generate new ones if the queue has less elements than {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} .
	 */
	void consume() {
		if (!pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			pipeQueue.removeFirst();
			while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
				pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step by inserting  {@code  pipe}  into the front of the queue.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to insert to front of queue.
	 */
	void undo(final Pipe pipe) {
		pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
	}
}
```

```java
/**
 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols.
 *
 * <p>
 * The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell.
 * The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell.
 * The source tile must not point into a wall.
 * The sink tile must point outside the map.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param rows Number of rows.
 * @param cols Number of columns.
 */
public Map(int rows, int cols) {
    this.rows = rows;
    this.cols = cols;
    this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
    
    // Initialize all cells as empty walls first
    for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
            cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
        }
    }
    
    // Generate source cell (non-edge, not pointing into wall)
    TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
    sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
    cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
    
    // Generate sink cell (edge, pointing outside)
    TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
    sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
    cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
}
```

Key points:
1. Initializes the grid with all Wall cells first
2. Uses the provided helper methods `generateStartCellInfo()` and `generateEndCellInfo()` to get valid positions and directions for the source and sink cells
3. Creates the source cell in a non-edge position (ensured by `generateStartCellInfo()`)
4. Creates the sink cell in an edge position pointing outward (ensured by `generateEndCellInfo()`)
5. Maintains all the constraints mentioned in the documentation

The helper methods already handle the complex logic of ensuring valid positions and directions, so we can safely use them in the constructor.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}
```

```java
/**
 * Creates a map with the given cells.
 *
 * <p>
 * The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell.
 * The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell.
 * The source tile must not point into a wall.
 * The sink tile must point outside the map.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param rows  Number of rows.
 * @param cols  Number of columns.
 * @param cells Cells to fill the map.
 */
public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
    this.rows = rows;
    this.cols = cols;
    this.cells = cells;
    
    // Validate the cells
    int sourceCount = 0;
    int sinkCount = 0;
    
    for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
            Cell cell = cells[i][j];
            if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
                if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
                    sourceCount++;
                    sourceCell = termCell;
                    
                    // Check source is in non-edge cell
                    if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
                    }
                    
                    // Check source doesn't point into a wall
                    Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                    if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols ||
                        cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
                    }
                } else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
                    sinkCount++;
                    sinkCell = termCell;
                    
                    // Check sink is in edge cell
                    if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
                    }
                    
                    // Check sink points outside map
                    Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                    if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    if (sourceCount != 1) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
    }
    
    if (sinkCount != 1) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
    }
}
```

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

/**
```
```java
 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
 *
 * <p>
 * Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a 
 * {@link FillableCell}.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param row One-Based row number to place pipe at.
 * @param col One-Based column number to place pipe at.
 * @param p   Pipe to place in cell.
 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
 */
boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
    // Convert to zero-based index
    int zeroRow = row - 1;
    int zeroCol = col - 1;
    
    // Check bounds
    if (zeroRow < 0 || zeroRow >= rows || zeroCol < 0 || zeroCol >= cols) {
        return false;
    }
    
    Cell targetCell = cells[zeroRow][zeroCol];
    
    // Check if cell is fillable and not already filled
    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
        if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
            fillableCell.setPipe(p);
            return true;
        }
    }
    
    return false;
```
```java
}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));

			}

			System.out.println();
		}

	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}
}
```

```java
/**
 * Map of the game.

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int zeroRow = row - 1;
		int zeroCol = col - 1;
		if (zeroRow < 0 || zeroRow >= rows || zeroCol < 0 || zeroCol >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[zeroRow][zeroCol];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}
```

Here's the complete method implementation:

```java
/**
 * Fills all pipes that are within {@code distance} units from the {@code sourceCell}.
 * 
 * <p>
 * Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling 
 * distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of 
 * the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param distance Distance to fill pipes.
 */
public void fillTiles(int distance) {
    if (distance < 0) {
        return;
    }
    
    // Save previous state to detect changes
    prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
    prevFilledDistance = distance;
    
    // Use BFS to fill cells within distance
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
    
    // Start from source cell
    queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
    distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int currentDist = distances.get(current);
        
        // Skip if beyond requested distance
        if (currentDist > distance) {
            continue;
        }
        
        // Fill current cell if it's fillable
        Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
            if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
                fillableCell.setFilled();
                filledTiles.add(current);
            }
        }
        
        // Explore adjacent cells
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
            
            // Check bounds
            if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || 
                neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Skip if already visited
            if (distances.containsKey(neighbor)) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Skip walls
            if (cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col] instanceof Wall) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Add to queue with distance+1
            distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
            queue.add(neighbor);
        }
    }
}
```

This implementation:
1. Uses BFS to explore cells starting from the source cell
2. Keeps track of distances from the source
3. Fills all FillableCells within the specified distance
4. Skips walls and out-of-bounds coordinates
5. Maintains the filledTiles set to track which cells have been filled
6. Updates prevFilledTiles and prevFilledDistance for game state tracking

The method will fill all reachable pipes within the given distance from the source cell, following the pipe connections and avoiding walls.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			break;
		} while (true);

	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;

			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	 * Displays the current map.

	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int zeroRow = row - 1;
		int zeroCol = col - 1;
		if (zeroRow < 0 || zeroRow >= rows || zeroCol < 0 || zeroCol >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[zeroRow][zeroCol];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		final Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not an instance of FillableCell");
		}
		FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
		fillableCell.removePipe();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}
}
```

/**
 * Fills all pipes that are within {@code distance} units from the {@code sourceCell}.
 * 
 * <p>
 * Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling 
 * distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of 
 * the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param distance Distance to fill pipes.
 */
public void fillTiles(int distance) {
    if (distance < 0) {
        return;
    }
    
    // Save previous state to detect changes
    prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
    prevFilledDistance = distance;
    
    // Use BFS to fill cells within distance
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
    
    // Start from source cell
    queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
    distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int currentDist = distances.get(current);
        
        // Skip if beyond requested distance
        if (currentDist > distance) {
            continue;
        }
        
        // Fill current cell if it's fillable
        Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
            if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
                fillableCell.setFilled();
                filledTiles.add(current);
            }
        }
        
        // Explore adjacent cells
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
            
            // Check bounds
            if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || 
                neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Skip if already visited
            if (distances.containsKey(neighbor)) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Skip walls
            if (cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col] instanceof Wall) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Add to queue with distance+1
            distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
            queue.add(neighbor);
        }
    }

```java
/**
 * Checks whether there exists a path from {@code sourceCell} to {@code sinkCell}.
 * 
 * <p>
 * The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal.
 * The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10.
 * </p>
 *
 * @return {@code true} if a path exists, else {@code false}.
 */
public boolean checkPath() {
    if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
        return false;
    }

    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
    
    queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
    visited.add(sourceCell.coord);

    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        
        // Check if we've reached the sink
        if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
            return true;
        }

        // Explore all possible directions
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
            
            // Skip if out of bounds or already visited
            if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || 
                neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols || 
                visited.contains(neighbor)) {
                continue;
            }

            Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
            Cell nextCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
            
            // Check if current cell can connect to neighbor
            if (canConnect(cell, dir) && canConnect(nextCell, dir.getOpposite())) {
                visited.add(neighbor);
                queue.add(neighbor);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}

// Helper method to check if a cell can connect in a given direction
private boolean canConnect(Cell cell, Direction dir) {
    if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
        TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
        return termCell.direction == dir;
    } else if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
        return fillableCell.isFilled() && fillableCell.getPipe().canConnect(dir);
    }
    return false;
}
```

This implementation:
1. Uses BFS to explore all possible paths from the source cell
2. Checks if each cell can connect to its neighbors in all four directions
3. Returns true if the sink cell is reached, false if all possibilities are exhausted without finding the sink
4. Includes a helper method `canConnect()` to check connection validity between cells

The method handles:
- Termination cells (source/sink) which only connect in their specified direction
- Fillable cells with pipes that must be filled and have the correct pipe connections
- Walls and other obstacles that block the path
- Boundary conditions to prevent out-of-bounds access

```java
	private final int cols;

	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull

	@NotNull

			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;

					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int zeroRow = row - 1;
		int zeroCol = col - 1;
		if (zeroRow < 0 || zeroRow >= rows || zeroCol < 0 || zeroCol >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[zeroRow][zeroCol];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		final Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not an instance of FillableCell");
		}
		FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
		fillableCell.removePipe();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	/**
	 * Fills all pipes that are within  {@code  distance}  units from the  {@code  sourceCell} . <p> Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling  distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of  the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same. </p>
	 * @param distance  Distance to fill pipes.
	 */
	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0) {
			return;
		}
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = distances.get(current);
			if (currentDist > distance) {
				continue;
			}
			Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
				FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
				if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(current);
				}
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols) {
					continue;
				}
				if (distances.containsKey(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col] instanceof Wall) {
					continue;
				}
				distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
				queue.add(neighbor);
			}
		}
	}
}
```

/**
 * Checks whether there exists a path from {@code sourceCell} to {@code sinkCell}.
 * 
 * <p>
 * The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal.
 * The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10.
 * </p>
 *
 * @return {@code true} if a path exists, else {@code false}.
 */
public boolean checkPath() {
    if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
        return false;
    }

    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
    
    queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
    visited.add(sourceCell.coord);

    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        
        // Check if we've reached the sink
        if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
            return true;
        }

        // Explore all possible directions
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
            
            // Skip if out of bounds or already visited
            if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || 
                neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols || 
                visited.contains(neighbor)) {
                continue;
            }

            Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
            Cell nextCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
            
            // Check if current cell can connect to neighbor
            if (canConnect(cell, dir) && canConnect(nextCell, dir.getOpposite())) {
                visited.add(neighbor);
                queue.add(neighbor);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}

// Helper method to check if a cell can connect in a given direction
private boolean canConnect(Cell cell, Direction dir) {
    if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
        TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
        return termCell.direction == dir;
    } else if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
        return fillableCell.isFilled() && fillableCell.getPipe().canConnect(dir);
    }
    return false;

```java
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int zeroRow = row - 1;
		int zeroCol = col - 1;
		if (zeroRow < 0 || zeroRow >= rows || zeroCol < 0 || zeroCol >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[zeroRow][zeroCol];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		final Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not an instance of FillableCell");
		}
		FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
		fillableCell.removePipe();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	/**
	 * Fills all pipes that are within  {@code  distance}  units from the  {@code  sourceCell} . <p> Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling  distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of  the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same. </p>
	 * @param distance  Distance to fill pipes.
	 */
	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0) {
			return;
		}
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = distances.get(current);
			if (currentDist > distance) {
				continue;
			}
			Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
				FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
				if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(current);
				}
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols) {
					continue;
				}
				if (distances.containsKey(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col] instanceof Wall) {
					continue;
				}
				distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
				queue.add(neighbor);
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether there exists a path from  {@code  sourceCell}  to  {@code  sinkCell} . <p> The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal. The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if a path exists, else  {@code  false} .
	 */
	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols
						|| visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
				Cell nextCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (canConnect(cell, dir) && canConnect(nextCell, dir.getOpposite())) {
					visited.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}
```
