```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	@NotNull
	private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {
		return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
	}

	/**
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: The game is lost when a round ends and no pipes are filled during the round. Is
	 * there a way to check whether pipes are filled during a round?
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.

	public boolean hasLost() {
		// TODO
		return false;

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int zeroRow = row - 1;
		int zeroCol = col - 1;
		if (zeroRow < 0 || zeroRow >= rows || zeroCol < 0 || zeroCol >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[zeroRow][zeroCol];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		final Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not an instance of FillableCell");
		}
		FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
		fillableCell.removePipe();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	/**
	 * Fills all pipes that are within  {@code  distance}  units from the  {@code  sourceCell} . <p> Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling  distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of  the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same. </p>
	 * @param distance  Distance to fill pipes.
	 */
	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0) {
			return;
		}
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = distances.get(current);
			if (currentDist > distance) {
				continue;
			}
			Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
				FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
				if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(current);
				}
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols) {
					continue;
				}
				if (distances.containsKey(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col] instanceof Wall) {
					continue;
				}
				distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
				queue.add(neighbor);
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether there exists a path from  {@code  sourceCell}  to  {@code  sinkCell} . <p> The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal. The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if a path exists, else  {@code  false} .
	 */
	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols
						|| visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
				Cell nextCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (canConnect(cell, dir) && canConnect(nextCell, dir.getOpposite())) {
					visited.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

```

Response Text:---
The error occurs because the `Map` class has constructor-like methods named `Map` (with uppercase M) instead of actual constructors (which should have the same name as the class). In Java, constructors must have the exact same name as the class (case-sensitive).

Here's the corrected `Map` class with proper constructors:

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    @NotNull
    private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    /**
     * Creates a map with size of rows x cols.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
                cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
            }
        }
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
        sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
        cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
        sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
        cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
    }

    /**
     * Creates a map with the given cells.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = cells;
        int sourceCount = 0;
        int sinkCount = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
                Cell cell = cells[i][j];
                if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
                    if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
                        sourceCount++;
                        sourceCell = termCell;
                        if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
                        }
                        Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                        if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
                                || cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
                        }
                    } else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
                        sinkCount++;
                        sinkCell = termCell;
                        if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
                        }
                        Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                        if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if (sourceCount != 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
        }
        if (sinkCount != 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
        }
    }

    // ... rest of the class remains unchanged ...
}
```

The key changes are:
1. Changed `void Map(int, int)` to `public Map(int, int)`
2. Changed `void Map(int, int, Cell[][])` to `public Map(int, int, Cell[][])`
3. Made them proper constructors by removing the return type and using the correct case for the class name

This should resolve the compilation errors about undefined constructors.

                        sinkCell = termCell;
                        if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
                        }
                        Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                        if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if (sourceCount != 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
        }
        if (sinkCount != 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
        }
    }

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	@NotNull
	private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {
		return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
	}

	/**
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: The game is lost when a round ends and no pipes are filled during the round. Is
	 * there a way to check whether pipes are filled during a round?
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		// TODO
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int zeroRow = row - 1;
		int zeroCol = col - 1;
		if (zeroRow < 0 || zeroRow >= rows || zeroCol < 0 || zeroCol >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[zeroRow][zeroCol];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		final Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not an instance of FillableCell");
		}
		FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
		fillableCell.removePipe();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	/**
	 * Fills all pipes that are within  {@code  distance}  units from the  {@code  sourceCell} . <p> Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling  distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of  the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same. </p>
	 * @param distance  Distance to fill pipes.
	 */
	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0) {
			return;
		}
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = distances.get(current);
			if (currentDist > distance) {
				continue;
			}
			Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
				FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
				if (!fillableCell.isFilled()) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(current);
				}
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols) {
					continue;
				}
				if (distances.containsKey(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col] instanceof Wall) {
					continue;
				}
				distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
				queue.add(neighbor);
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether there exists a path from  {@code  sourceCell}  to  {@code  sinkCell} . <p> The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal. The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if a path exists, else  {@code  false} .
	 */
	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols
						|| visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[current.row][current.col];
				Cell nextCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (canConnect(cell, dir) && canConnect(nextCell, dir.getOpposite())) {
					visited.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}
```

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    @NotNull
    private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    /**
     * Creates a map with size of rows x cols.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
                cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
            }
        }
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
        sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
        cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
        sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
        cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
    }

    /**
     * Creates a map with the given cells.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = cells;
        int sourceCount = 0;
        int sinkCount = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
                Cell cell = cells[i][j];
                if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
                    if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
                        sourceCount++;
                        sourceCell = termCell;
                        if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
                        }
                        Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                        if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
                                || cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
                        }
                    } else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
                        sinkCount++;
                        sinkCell = termCell;
                        if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
                        }
                        Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                        if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if (sourceCount != 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell");
        }
        if (sinkCount != 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell");
        }
    }

    // ... rest of the class remains unchanged ...
}

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;

import util.Direction;

public class Map {
    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull final Cell[][] cells;
    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;
    @NotNull private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        // Initialize cells and termination cells
    }

    public Map(int rows, int cols, @NotNull Cell[][] cells) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = cells;
        // Validate termination cells
    }

    // Rest of the class implementation...
}
```

The key changes are:
1. Removed the `void` return type from constructors
2. Made constructors public
3. Kept the same parameter lists but properly implemented them as constructors

The rest of the class implementation should remain the same. This should resolve the compilation errors about undefined constructors.

Based on the task description and the provided code, the `toSingleChar()` method should return a character representation of a termination cell (either source or sink) based on its type and direction. The hint suggests using `PipePatterns` utility class.

Here's the completed method:

```java
/**
 * <p>
 * Hint: use {@link util.PipePatterns}
 * </p>
 *
 * @return the character representation of a termination cell in game
 */
@Override
public char toSingleChar() {
    return type == Type.SOURCE 
        ? PipePatterns.Characters.SOURCE.getChar(pointingTo)
        : PipePatterns.Characters.SINK.getChar(pointingTo);
}
```

This implementation:
1. Checks the `type` of the termination cell (SOURCE or SINK)
2. Uses the appropriate enum from `PipePatterns.Characters` (SOURCE or SINK)
3. Gets the corresponding character based on the direction (`pointingTo`)
4. Returns the character representation

The method assumes that `PipePatterns.Characters` has appropriate enum values with a `getChar(Direction)` method that returns the correct character for each direction.

    }
}

   - Vertical pipes connect up and down

   - Cross pipes connect in all four directions

Here's the complete method:

```java
/**
 * Converts a String to a Pipe.
 *
 * <p>
 * Here is the list of ASCII representation to the pipes:
 * TL: Top-Left
 * TR: Top-Right
 * BL: Bottom-Left
 * BR: Bottom-Right
 * HZ: Horizontal
 * VT: Vertical
 * CR: Cross
 * </p>
 *
 * @param rep String representation of the pipe. For example, "HZ" corresponds to a pipe of horizontal shape.
 * @return Pipe identified by the string.
 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the String does not represent a known pipe.
 */
public static Pipe fromString(String rep) {
    if (rep == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("String representation cannot be null");
    }
    
    Shape shape;
    switch (rep.toUpperCase()) {
        case "HZ":
            shape = Shape.HORIZONTAL;
            break;
        case "VT":
            shape = Shape.VERTICAL;
            break;
        case "TL":
            shape = Shape.TOP_LEFT;
            break;
        case "TR":
            shape = Shape.TOP_RIGHT;
            break;
        case "BL":
            shape = Shape.BOTTOM_LEFT;
            break;
        case "BR":
            shape = Shape.BOTTOM_RIGHT;
            break;
        case "CR":
            shape = Shape.CROSS;
            break;
        default:
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown pipe representation: " + rep);
    }
    
    return new Pipe(shape);
}
```

The method:
1. Checks for null input
2. Uses a switch statement to map string codes to Shape enum values
3. Throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown codes
4. Returns a new Pipe with the appropriate shape
5. Converts input to uppercase to make the matching case-insensitive

```java
package game.pipes;

import game.MapElement;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Direction;
import util.PipePatterns;

public class Pipe implements MapElement {

	@NotNull
	private final Shape shape;
	private boolean filled = false;

	/**
	 * Converts a String to a Pipe.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Here is the list of ASCII representation to the pipes:
	 * TL: Top-Left
	 * TR: Top-Right
	 * BL: Bottom-Left
	 * BR: Bottom-Right
	 * HZ: Horizontal
	 * VT: Vertical
	 * CR: Cross
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rep String representation of the pipe. For example, "HZ" corresponds to a pipe of horizontal shape.
	 * @return Pipe identified by the string.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the String does not represent a known pipe.
	 */
	public static Pipe fromString(String rep) {
		// TODO
	}

	public enum Shape {
		HORIZONTAL(PipePatterns.Filled.HORIZONTAL, PipePatterns.Unfilled.HORIZONTAL),
		VERTICAL(PipePatterns.Filled.VERTICAL, PipePatterns.Unfilled.VERTICAL),
		TOP_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_LEFT),
		TOP_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_RIGHT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_RIGHT),
		BOTTOM_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_LEFT),
		BOTTOM_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_RIGHT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_RIGHT),
		CROSS(PipePatterns.Filled.CROSS, PipePatterns.Unfilled.CROSS);

		final char filledChar;
		final char unfilledChar;

		Shape(char filled, char unfilled) {
			this.filledChar = filled;
			this.unfilledChar = unfilled;
		}

		char getCharByState(boolean isFilled) {
			return isFilled ? filledChar : unfilledChar;
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a new pipe with a given shape.
	 * @param shape  Shape of the pipe.
	 */
	public void Pipe(@NotNull Shape shape) {
		this.shape = shape;
	}

	/**
	 * Sets the pipe as filled.
	 */
	public void setFilled() {
		this.filled = true;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  Whether this pipe is filled.
	 */
	public boolean getFilled() {
		return filled;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  List of connections for this pipe.
	 * @throws IllegalStateException  if  {@code  this}  pipe cannot be identified.
	 */
	public Direction[] getConnections() {
		switch (shape) {
		case HORIZONTAL:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
		case VERTICAL:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN };
		case TOP_LEFT:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.LEFT };
		case TOP_RIGHT:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.RIGHT };
		case BOTTOM_LEFT:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT };
		case BOTTOM_RIGHT:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.RIGHT };
		case CROSS:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
		default:
			throw new IllegalStateException("Pipe cannot be identified");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The character representation of this pipe. Note that the representation is different for filled and unfilled pipes.
	 */
	@Override
	public char toSingleChar() {
		return shape.getCharByState(filled);
	}
}
```

I'll help complete the `start()` method for the JesonMor game class. The method needs to implement the game loop where players take turns making moves until there's a winner.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();
    
    while (true) {
        // Get players in order
        Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
        
        // Iterate through each player for their turn
        for (Player player : players) {
            this.currentPlayer = player;
            
            // Get available moves for current player
            Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(player);
            
            // If no moves available, skip this player
            if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Get player's move choice
            Move chosenMove = player.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
            
            // Execute the move
            movePiece(chosenMove);
            this.numMoves++;
            
            // Update score and check for winner
            updateScore(player, board[chosenMove.to().x()][chosenMove.to().y()], chosenMove);
            winner = getWinner(player, board[chosenMove.to().x()][chosenMove.to().y()], chosenMove);
            
            // Refresh output after each move
            this.refreshOutput();
            
            // If we have a winner, break out of the loop
            if (winner != null) {
                break;
            }
        }
        
        if (winner != null) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
            System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
            return winner;
        }
    }
}
```

This implementation:
1. Gets the players in order from the configuration
2. For each player in turn:
   - Sets the current player
   - Gets all available moves
   - Gets the player's chosen move
   - Executes the move
   - Updates the score
   - Checks for a winner
   - Refreshes the output
3. If a winner is found, breaks out of the loop and returns the winner
4. Continues the loop until a winner is found

The method follows all the requirements mentioned in the documentation, including using the specified methods (`nextMove`, `refreshOutput`) and maintaining the correct player order.

I'll help complete the `getWinner` method for the JesonMor game. Based on the context, this method should determine if the last player who made a move has won the game.

The method should:
1. Check if the last player has reached a winning condition
2. Return the winning player if conditions are met, otherwise return null

Since this appears to be a knight's move game (JesonMor), a common winning condition would be when a player's knight reaches the opposite side of the board (similar to reaching the other side in chess).

Here's the implementation:

```java
@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // Check if the moved piece is a Knight (assuming Knight is the winning piece)
    if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
        int boardWidth = board.length;
        int boardHeight = board[0].length;
        
        // For player 1 (starting at bottom), winning is reaching top row (y = boardHeight-1)
        // For player 2 (starting at top), winning is reaching bottom row (y = 0)
        int targetRow = lastPlayer.equals(configuration.getPlayers()[0]) ? boardHeight - 1 : 0;
        
        if (lastMove.to().y() == targetRow) {
            return lastPlayer;
        }
    }
    return null;
}
```

This implementation:
1. Checks if the moved piece is a Knight (since only Knights can win)
2. Determines the target row based on which player is moving
3. Returns the player if their Knight reached the opposite side
4. Returns null otherwise

The method assumes:
- The game has two players
- Player 1 starts at the bottom (y=0) and needs to reach the top
- Player 2 starts at the top and needs to reach the bottom
- Only Knights can win the game by reaching the opposite side

You may need to adjust the target row logic if your game configuration differs.

I'll help complete the `updateScore` method. The task is to calculate the Manhattan distance between the source and destination places of a move, then add this distance to the player's current score.

The Manhattan distance is calculated as:
`distance = |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|`

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
/**
 * Update the score of a player according to the {@link Piece} and corresponding move made by him just now.
 * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score
 * of this player.
 * <p>
 * The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes.
 * The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination {@link Place}.
 * <p>
 * Student can use {@link Player#getScore()} to get the current score of a player before updating.
 * {@link Player#setScore(int)} can be used to update the score of a player.
 * <p>
 * <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
 *
 * @param player the player who just makes a move
 * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
 * @param move   the move that is just made
 */
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    Place source = move.from();
    Place destination = move.to();
    int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
    int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
    player.setScore(newScore);
}
```

This implementation:
1. Gets the source and destination places from the move
2. Calculates the Manhattan distance between them
3. Gets the player's current score and adds the distance to it
4. Updates the player's score with the new value

The method follows all the requirements mentioned in the documentation, including using the Manhattan distance and properly updating the player's score.

```java
/**
 * Get all available moves of one player.
 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
 * <p>
 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
 *
 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
 * @return an array of available moves
 */
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> allMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    
    // Iterate through the entire board
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            // Check if the piece belongs to the player
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                // Get available moves for this piece
                Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace);
                // Add all valid moves to the list
                allMoves.addAll(Arrays.asList(pieceMoves));
            }
        }
    }
    
    return allMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

This implementation:
1. Uses an ArrayList to dynamically collect moves since we don't know how many there will be
2. Scans the entire board for pieces belonging to the given player
3. For each found piece, gets its available moves from its current position
4. Collects all moves and converts them to an array before returning
5. Returns an empty array if no moves are available

The method ensures all returned moves are valid by relying on the `Piece#getAvailableMoves()` implementation of each piece class to return only valid moves.

```java
	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		while (true) {
			Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
			for (Player player : players) {
				this.currentPlayer = player;
				Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(player);
				if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
					continue;
				}
				Move chosenMove = player.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
				movePiece(chosenMove);
				this.numMoves++;
				updateScore(player, board[chosenMove.to().x()][chosenMove.to().y()], chosenMove);
				winner = getWinner(player, board[chosenMove.to().x()][chosenMove.to().y()], chosenMove);
				this.refreshOutput();
				if (winner != null) {
					break;
				}
			}
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
			int boardWidth = board.length;
			int boardHeight = board[0].length;
			int targetRow = lastPlayer.equals(configuration.getPlayers()[0]) ? boardHeight - 1 : 0;
			if (lastMove.to().y() == targetRow) {
				return lastPlayer;
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	/**

The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination  {@link Place} . <p> Student can use  {@link Player#getScore()}  to get the current score of a player before updating. {@link Player#setScore(int)}  can be used to update the score of a player. <p> <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
	 * @param player  the player who just makes a move
	 * @param piece   the piece that is just moved
	 * @param move    the move that is just made
	 */
	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.from();
		Place destination = move.to();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
```

```java
package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.protocol.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
	public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
		super(configuration);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		while (true) {
			Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
			for (Player player : players) {
				this.currentPlayer = player;
				Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(player);
				if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
					continue;
				}
				Move chosenMove = player.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
				movePiece(chosenMove);
				this.numMoves++;
				updateScore(player, board[chosenMove.to().x()][chosenMove.to().y()], chosenMove);
				winner = getWinner(player, board[chosenMove.to().x()][chosenMove.to().y()], chosenMove);
				this.refreshOutput();
				if (winner != null) {
					break;
				}
			}
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
			int boardWidth = board.length;
			int boardHeight = board[0].length;
			int targetRow = lastPlayer.equals(configuration.getPlayers()[0]) ? boardHeight - 1 : 0;
			if (lastMove.to().y() == targetRow) {
				return lastPlayer;
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	/**
	 * Update the score of a player according to the  {@link Piece}  and corresponding move made by him just now. This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score of this player. <p> The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes. The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination  {@link Place} . <p> Student can use  {@link Player#getScore()}  to get the current score of a player before updating. {@link Player#setScore(int)}  can be used to update the score of a player. <p> <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
	 * @param player  the player who just makes a move
	 * @param piece   the piece that is just moved
	 * @param move    the move that is just made
	 */
	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.from();
		Place destination = move.to();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

	/**
	 * Make a move. This method performs moving a  {@link Piece}  from source to destination  {@link Place}  according  {@link Move}  object. Note that after the move, there will be no  {@link Piece}  in source  {@link Place} . <p> Positions of all  {@link Piece} s on the gameboard are stored in  {@link JesonMor#board}  field as a 2-dimension array of {@link Piece}  objects. The x and y coordinate of a  {@link Place}  on the gameboard are used as index in  {@link JesonMor#board} . E.g.  {@code  board[place.x()][place.y()]} . If one  {@link Place}  does not have a piece on it, it will be null in  {@code  board[place.x()][place.y()]} . Student may modify elements in  {@link JesonMor#board}  to implement moving a  {@link Piece} . The  {@link Move}  object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
	 * @param move  the move to make
	 */
	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place from = move.from();
		Place to = move.to();
		Piece piece = board[from.x()][from.y()];
		board[to.x()][to.y()] = piece;
		board[from.x()][from.y()] = null;
	}
}
```

- BOT: 
/**
 * Get all available moves of one player.
 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
 * <p>
 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
 *
 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
 * @return an array of available moves
 */
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> allMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    
    // Iterate through the entire board
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            // Check if the piece belongs to the player
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                // Get available moves for this piece
                Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace);
                // Add all valid moves to the list
                allMoves.addAll(Arrays.asList(pieceMoves));
            }
        }
    }
    
    return allMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

Response Text:---
The error indicates that the `Move` class is missing `from()` and `to()` methods that are being called in multiple places in the `JesonMor` class. Here's the correct implementation of the `Move` class that should resolve these compilation errors:

```java
package assignment.protocol;

public class Move {
    private final Place from;
    private final Place to;

    public Move(Place from, Place to) {
        this.from = from;
        this.to = to;
    }

    public Place from() {
        return from;
    }

    public Place to() {
        return to;
    }
}
```

Explanation:
1. The `Move` class needs to store both source (`from`) and destination (`to`) positions as `Place` objects
2. It needs getter methods `from()` and `to()` that return these positions
3. The constructor takes both positions as parameters
4. This implementation matches the usage in the `JesonMor` class where these methods are being called

This should resolve all the compilation errors related to missing `from()` and `to()` methods in the `Move` class.

```java
			for (Player player : players) {
				this.currentPlayer = player;
				Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(player);
				if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
					continue;
				}
				Move chosenMove = player.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
				movePiece(chosenMove);
				this.numMoves++;
				updateScore(player, board[chosenMove.to().x()][chosenMove.to().y()], chosenMove);
				winner = getWinner(player, board[chosenMove.to().x()][chosenMove.to().y()], chosenMove);
				this.refreshOutput();
				if (winner != null) {
					break;
				}
			}
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
			int boardWidth = board.length;
			int boardHeight = board[0].length;
			int targetRow = lastPlayer.equals(configuration.getPlayers()[0]) ? boardHeight - 1 : 0;
			if (lastMove.to().y() == targetRow) {
				return lastPlayer;
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	/**
	 * Update the score of a player according to the  {@link Piece}  and corresponding move made by him just now. This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score of this player. <p> The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes. The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination  {@link Place} . <p> Student can use  {@link Player#getScore()}  to get the current score of a player before updating. {@link Player#setScore(int)}  can be used to update the score of a player. <p> <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
	 * @param player  the player who just makes a move
	 * @param piece   the piece that is just moved
	 * @param move    the move that is just made
	 */
	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.from();
		Place destination = move.to();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

	/**
	 * Make a move. This method performs moving a  {@link Piece}  from source to destination  {@link Place}  according  {@link Move}  object. Note that after the move, there will be no  {@link Piece}  in source  {@link Place} . <p> Positions of all  {@link Piece} s on the gameboard are stored in  {@link JesonMor#board}  field as a 2-dimension array of {@link Piece}  objects. The x and y coordinate of a  {@link Place}  on the gameboard are used as index in  {@link JesonMor#board} . E.g.  {@code  board[place.x()][place.y()]} . If one  {@link Place}  does not have a piece on it, it will be null in  {@code  board[place.x()][place.y()]} . Student may modify elements in  {@link JesonMor#board}  to implement moving a  {@link Piece} . The  {@link Move}  object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
	 * @param move  the move to make
	 */
	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place from = move.from();
		Place to = move.to();
		Piece piece = board[from.x()][from.y()];
		board[to.x()][to.y()] = piece;
		board[from.x()][from.y()] = null;
	}
}
```

/**
 * Get all available moves of one player.
 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
 * <p>
 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
 *
 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
 * @return an array of available moves
 */
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> allMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    
    // Iterate through the entire board
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            // Check if the piece belongs to the player
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                // Get available moves for this piece
                Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace);
                // Add all valid moves to the list
                allMoves.addAll(Arrays.asList(pieceMoves));
            }
        }
    }
    
    return allMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

Response Text:---
The error indicates that the `Move` class is missing the `from()` and `to()` methods that are being called throughout the code. Here's the corrected `Move` class implementation:

```java
package assignment.protocol;

public class Move {
    private final Place from;
    private final Place to;

    public Move(Place from, Place to) {
        this.from = from;
        this.to = to;
    }

    public Place from() {
        return this.from;
    }

    public Place to() {
        return this.to;
    }
}
```

This implementation provides the required accessor methods `from()` and `to()` that return the `Place` objects representing the move's source and destination positions. The class maintains immutability by making the fields final and only providing accessors without mutators.

I'll help complete the `createGame` method according to the requirements. The method should:
1. Create two players (user and computer)
2. Create a Configuration with these players
3. Add initial pieces to the gameboard following assignment requirements
4. Return a JesonMor game object

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    // Create players
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    
    // Create configuration with user player first
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, 
        new Player[]{userPlayer, computerPlayer}, numMovesProtection);
    
    // Add initial pieces according to assignment requirements
    // User pieces
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), 0, 0);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), 0, 1);
    
    // Computer pieces
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), size-1, size-1);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), size-1, size-2);
    
    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

Key points about this implementation:
1. Places user player first in the array (as required)
2. Adds both Knight and Archer pieces for each player
3. Positions user pieces at top-left (0,0 and 0,1) and computer pieces at bottom-right (size-1,size-1 and size-1,size-2)
4. Maintains proper spacing between pieces
5. Returns a properly initialized JesonMor game object

The implementation assumes standard chess-like starting positions but you may need to adjust the exact positions based on your specific assignment requirements.

I'll help complete the `getAvailableMoves` method for the Knight class. The method should return all valid L-shaped moves (like in chess) from the current position, considering the game board boundaries and other validation rules.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    
    // All possible L-shaped moves for a knight (8 possible directions)
    int[] rowOffsets = {-2, -2, -1, -1, 1, 1, 2, 2};
    int[] colOffsets = {-1, 1, -2, 2, -2, 2, -1, 1};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < rowOffsets.length; i++) {
        int newRow = source.getRow() + rowOffsets[i];
        int newCol = source.getColumn() + colOffsets[i];
        Place destination = new Place(newRow, newCol);
        Move move = new Move(source, destination);
        
        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
            validMoves.add(move);
        }
    }
    
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

Explanation:
1. The method generates all 8 possible L-shaped moves a knight can make in chess (2 squares in one direction and then 1 square perpendicular).
2. For each potential move, it creates a new Move object with the source and calculated destination.
3. It uses the existing `validateMove` method to check if each move is valid according to all game rules.
4. Valid moves are collected in an ArrayList and converted to an array before returning.
5. The method handles edge cases (like moves that would go off the board) through the validation rules.

The implementation ensures all returned moves are valid according to the game's rules, including boundary checks and other constraints defined in the validation rules.

```java
/**
 * Knight piece that moves similar to knight in chess.

 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)'>Wikipedia</a>
 */

	public Knight(Player player) {
		super(player);
	}

	@Override
	public char getLabel() {
		return 'K';
	}

	 * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.

	 * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
	 * All the returned {@link Move} should have source equal to the source parameter.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
	 * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game   the game object
	 * @param source the current place of the piece
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	@Override
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new KnightMoveRule(),
				new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}
```

Response Text:---
Here's the completed `validate` method for the `OccupiedRule` class. This method checks if the destination square of the move contains a piece belonging to the same player as the moving piece, which would make the move invalid.

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    // Get the piece at the destination position
    Piece destinationPiece = game.getPieceAt(move.getDestination());
    
    // If there's no piece at the destination, the move is valid
    if (destinationPiece == null) {
        return true;
    }
    
    // Get the moving piece
    Piece movingPiece = game.getPieceAt(move.getOrigin());
    
    // If the moving piece and destination piece belong to the same player, the move is invalid
    return movingPiece.getPlayer() != destinationPiece.getPlayer();
}
```

Explanation:
1. The method first checks if there's a piece at the destination position.
2. If there's no piece, the move is automatically valid (return true).
3. If there is a piece, it checks if the moving piece and destination piece belong to different players.
4. The move is valid only if the pieces belong to different players (return true), otherwise invalid (return false).

This implementation follows the rule's description that "a piece cannot be captured by another piece belonging to the same player".

Response Text:---
I'll help complete the `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Archer` class. Based on the Wikipedia link provided, an Archer (Cannon) moves like a Rook (horizontally or vertically any number of squares), but captures by jumping over exactly one piece of any color along the path.

Here's the implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}}; // 4 possible directions
    
    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int dx = dir[0];
        int dy = dir[1];
        int x = source.getX() + dx;
        int y = source.getY() + dy;
        boolean foundPiece = false;
        
        // Keep moving in the direction until out of bounds
        while (game.getBoard().isValidPlace(x, y)) {
            Place dest = new Place(x, y);
            Move move = new Move(source, dest);
            
            // For non-capture moves (must have no pieces in between)
            if (!foundPiece) {
                if (game.getBoard().getPiece(dest) == null) {
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                } else {
                    foundPiece = true; // Found first piece
                }
            } 
            // For capture moves (must jump over exactly one piece)
            else {
                if (game.getBoard().getPiece(dest) != null) {
                    // Check if destination has opponent's piece
                    if (game.getBoard().getPiece(dest).getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                    break; // Can't jump over more than one piece
                }
            }
            
            x += dx;
            y += dy;
        }
    }
    
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

Explanation:
1. The method checks all 4 possible directions (up, down, left, right)
2. For each direction, it scans squares until it goes out of bounds
3. For non-capture moves (moving without jumping):
   - The path must be completely clear
   - Valid moves are added to the list
4. For capture moves (jumping over exactly one piece):
   - Must find exactly one piece to jump over
   - The destination must contain an opponent's piece
   - Valid capture moves are added to the list
5. All moves are validated using the existing `validateMove` method
6. Returns an array of all valid moves

The implementation follows the Cannon movement rules from Chinese Chess where it can:
- Move like a Rook when not capturing
- Capture by jumping over exactly one piece (of any color) to take an opponent's piece

```java
	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
```

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};
    
    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int dx = dir[0];
        int dy = dir[1];
        int x = source.x() + dx;
        int y = source.y() + dy;
        boolean foundPiece = false;
```
        
```java
        while (x >= 0 && x < game.getBoardWidth() && y >= 0 && y < game.getBoardHeight()) {
            Place dest = new Place(x, y);
            Move move = new Move(source, dest);
            
            if (!foundPiece) {
                if (game.getPiece(dest) == null) {
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                } else {
                    foundPiece = true;
                }
            } else {
                if (game.getPiece(dest) != null) {
                    if (game.getPiece(dest).getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
            
            x += dx;
            y += dy;
        }
    }
    
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

I'll help complete the `validate` method for the `FirstNMovesProtectionRule` class. This rule should prevent piece captures during the first N moves of the game.

Explanation:
The method should:
1. Check if the current move number is within the protected range (numProtectedMoves)
2. If it is, verify that the move doesn't capture a piece
3. Return true if the move is valid, false otherwise

Here's the complete method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    // Get current move number (1-based)
    int currentMoveNumber = game.getMoveHistory().size() + 1;
    
    // If we're within protected moves and the move captures a piece, it's invalid
    if (currentMoveNumber <= numProtectedMoves && move.getCapturedPiece() != null) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // Otherwise, the move is valid
    return true;
}
```

This implementation:
- Checks if the current move is within the protected range (<= numProtectedMoves)
- Verifies if the move would capture a piece (move.getCapturedPiece() != null)
- Returns false only if both conditions are true (protected move AND capture attempt)
- Returns true in all other cases (either not protected move or not a capture)

Here's the completed `validate` method for the `KnightMoveRule` class. This implementation checks if a knight's move follows the standard L-shaped pattern (2 squares in one direction and then 1 square perpendicular, or vice versa):

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }
    
    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getColumn();
    int targetRow = move.getTarget().getRow();
    int targetCol = move.getTarget().getColumn();
    
    int rowDiff = Math.abs(targetRow - sourceRow);
    int colDiff = Math.abs(targetCol - sourceCol);
    
    // Knight moves in L-shape: (2,1) or (1,2)
    return (rowDiff == 2 && colDiff == 1) || (rowDiff == 1 && colDiff == 2);
}
```

Explanation:
1. First checks if the moving piece is a Knight (existing check)
2. Gets source and target positions
3. Calculates absolute differences in rows and columns
4. Returns true if the move follows either of the two valid L-shaped patterns:
   - 2 squares in one direction and 1 square perpendicular
   - 1 square in one direction and 2 squares perpendicular

This implementation correctly validates knight moves according to standard chess rules.

- The `!` operator negates the result of the equality check to align with the rule's requirement.  

This implementation ensures the move is only valid if the source and destination are different.
